model_descriptions.lr_pair_scorer: A tiny, permutation-invariant, mask-exact scorer for one (L,R,A->B) triple. For each triple it computes a fixed (non-learned) bank of masked statistics over its contact cells. These include tie-averaged rank transforms of the ligand row (row 0) and receptor row (row 1), a plain masked Spearman correlation, and a covariate-adjusted partial Spearman. The partial version residualises both ranked rows on [1, row2 library offset, row3 sender fraction] by closed-form masked ridge least squares. It then converts that correlation to a sqrt(n-3)*atanh(r) z-statistic, so the large contact-cell counts of weak-effect triples add evidence. Further features are a row3-weighted correlation, a top-vs-bottom ligand-tercile receptor contrast, nuisance diagnostics (correlations of R and L with rows 2 and 3), and log n. A 2-hidden-layer MLP (width 32) maps the standardised features to a score. A learned scalar skip from the partial-Spearman z-statistic means the model starts as a covariate-adjusted Spearman ranker. The output is an unbounded scalar per triple, trained with smooth_l1 against the 0/1 target (the run is regression-typed).

key_findings: Best lr_auprc is 0.5643 (record lr_pair_scorer_loop2b_002, Formal, 5,122 params). That is about 5x the ~0.11 random level. It is the only Formal score at that value, so it is not independent replication.

Round 1 scored 0.5604 with 1,538 params. Round 2 scored 0.5643 with 5,122 params. The gain is +0.0039 (+0.7%), within plausible seed noise. With one seed per round, the extra capacity (hidden_dim 64, 3.3x params) is not shown to help.

Secondary metrics are strong and consistent with the primary score. lr_auroc is 0.868 and direction_accuracy is 0.788. In round 1, AUROC was 0.866 and direction_accuracy about 0.80. Direction accuracy was slightly lower in round 2 even though AUPRC rose. So the round-2 change did not improve direction.

The performance mostly comes from the fixed statistic bank, not from learning. These features are masked rank transforms, covariate-adjusted partial Spearman z-statistic, and a learned skip. The model starts as a covariate-adjusted Spearman ranker. The small MLP adds little beyond that. This design explains the high score relative to the plain-Spearman baseline, but the run has no baseline score to quantify the margin.

Training is stable and healthy. Train loss fell 0.0341→0.0206 and val loss fell 0.0234→0.0216 over 25 epochs. Best epoch was 20 and the last-epoch val loss was only +4.3e-5 above best. The train/val gap was +0.00095, which is comparable, so there was no overfitting. The loss was still creeping down at the end, so the model is close to converged under this schedule.
Health gates passed in both rounds (continue=2). There were no failures.
bottlenecks: The scorer's ceiling is set by the hand-designed, fixed feature bank. Partial Spearman on contact cells carries most of the signal, and the MLP has little room to add to it.

The confound that the task builds in is probably the main limit. Every other receptor × sender × receiver combination gets an equally sized perturbation from an unobserved ligand, so contact-cell correlation cannot fully separate injected from decoy triples. This is a hypothesis, not tested here.
Capacity is not the bottleneck. Moving from 1.5k to 5.1k params changed the score by 0.004.

The smooth_l1 regression loss on a 0/1 target at about 7% prevalence is not a ranking loss. It does not optimise AP directly. Validation loss was used for checkpoint selection, not lr_auprc. Neither point was tested in this run.
Only 2 rounds, each with a single seed and no ablations. Noise cannot be separated from signal, and the contribution of each feature is not known.
lr_pair_scorer.best_config_analysis: The best config used hidden_dim 64, 2 layers, ridge 1e-3, covariates on, learned skip, feature_clip 8, min_contacts 4, dropout 0, AdamW at lr 2e-3 with weight decay 1e-5, cosine schedule over 25 epochs, and smooth_l1. Most of the benefit likely comes from design choices that were present in both rounds: the covariate-adjusted partial Spearman z-statistic, the sqrt(n-3) weighting, and the skip initialisation. The round-2 change (wider MLP) only added +0.004, which is not distinguishable from noise. The cosine schedule and best-validation-loss checkpointing gave stable convergence, with best epoch 20 of 25. Which hyperparameter mattered most cannot be established, because no one-at-a-time ablation was run.
lr_pair_scorer.score_trend: The trend is flat to marginally up: 0.5604 → 0.5643. There are only two points, so the model looks plateaued at about 0.56. A larger run is unlikely to give big gains from capacity alone. Any further gains would have to come from new features or a different loss.
lr_pair_scorer.per_file_analysis: No per-sample evidence is available. The summary has only aggregate scores, with no per-dataset or per-tile score table. 2,214 validation rows were materialised, but no per-dataset results were given. So nothing can be said about variation across the 21 validation datasets, the 7 tiles, or beta levels.
lr_pair_scorer.data_sensitivity: Data sensitivity cannot be measured. Both rounds were Formal, with operator-fixed full training and evaluation portions (formal_train_portion 1.0, formal_eval_portion 1.0) over 60 training datasets. No Trial records exist (Trial=0, Formal=2), so no Trial/Formal comparison or trial-vs-formal gap is available. The small train/val gap (+0.00095) suggests low variance, so more data is unlikely to matter much for such a small model.
lr_pair_scorer.efficiency_assessment: The model is very cheap. It has 5,122 params in the best config, against 1,538 in round 1. Training took 161.4 s including 35.0 s of validation. Inference took 5.5 s, scoring 1.9 s, and peak GPU memory was 83 MiB in training and 140 MiB at inference. The 1.5k-param round-1 model reaches 0.5604, 99.3% of the best score, so the simpler config is the better cost-performance choice unless the +0.004 gain is shown to be real. The training time of round 1 is not given.
lr_pair_scorer.strategy_assessment: The exploration was thin. The run had 2 rounds, both Formal, because the operator forced formal rounds. It did not follow a screening→refinement→solidification sequence. There were no Trial rounds, no seed repeats, no ablations of features or loss, and no comparison to the Spearman baseline. The agent changed capacity alone and reported a gain that it itself judged to be possibly noise. A better strategy would be to test untried levers, such as a ranking or BCE loss, feature ablations, and several seeds, and to report the margin over the baseline.

runtime_vocab.name: score_lr_pair_scorer_vs_sota
runtime_vocab.description: lr_pair_scorer scored 0.5643, within 5% of SOTA (0.5643). Competitive but not a clear improvement.

runtime_vocab.name: beta_weighted_loss
runtime_vocab.description: Per-positive training-loss weight that increases as the injected effect size beta decreases. This upweights the weak-effect (beta=0.5) positives that the Spearman baseline misses. Requires beta labels at training time only.

runtime_vocab.name: covariate_adjusted_pair_scoring
runtime_vocab.description: Score each (L, R, A->B) triple from the ligand row and receptor row relationship. Library offset and sender-neighbour fraction enter as covariates. No batch-relative normalization is used.

runtime_vocab.name: masked_padding_pooling
runtime_vocab.description: Mask-aware pooling over a variable number of contact cells or triples, so padded entries are excluded from every aggregate and from the loss.

prediction_evaluation.notes: Prediction not evaluated: no SOTA baseline was available (metric='lr_auprc', resolution='bound_id').
